definition: A flow of electric charge, measured in amperes (A) with an ammeter connected in series; Extended students also define it as the charge passing a point each second, $I = \frac{Q}{t}$.
A meter that measures electric current; it is connected in series with the part of the circuit being measured and has a very small resistance.
Current that flows round a circuit in one direction only, such as the current from a cell or battery; it is d.c. even if its size changes.
Current that keeps reversing its direction, such as the current from the mains supply, which reverses many times each second.
The direction chosen for current: from the positive terminal of the supply, round the circuit outside it, to the negative terminal; free electrons flow the opposite way.
